newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Latin shares mixed on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Latin shares mixed on U.S. data.

text.p: Latin American shares were mixed in U.S. trade on Thursday, helped by tame U.S. inflation and weighed by delays facing an Argentine fiscal package, analysts said.

The U.S. Producer Price Index for August showed an increase of 0.3 percent, and jobless claims also were higher than expected. The data encouraged investors to shift to interest-sensitive Latin stocks and away from Treasury bonds.
"The stocks really are rather mixed. The U.S. news is being taken as a moderate positive," one trader said.
Among Latin American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), Argentina's YPF Sociedad rose on a newspaper report Spanish oil company Repsol SA might take a stake in the company.
YPF rose in the early afternoon to 22-7/8, up 1/4, on volume of 940,200 shares.

However, analysts said other Argentine stocks were being hurt by the Argentine Congress' delay late on Wednesday of a vote on a fiscal adjustment package sought by President Carlos Menem. Argentina's vice president said on Thursday he expected the lower house to approve the measure this week.

Brazilian stocks were boosted by prospects Brazil's lower house would pass legislation exempting exports from states' so-called ICMS tax and a bill aimed at trimming the federal workforce. Shares in state telecommunications company Telebras rose to 77-1/8 up 1/2.
Swedish telecommunications company LM Ericsson and Finland's Nokia Group were helped by downgrades of Motorola Inc stock by three investment houses.
Analysts said the Nordic telecoms could see their market share increase with the damage to Motorola. Nokia was unchanged at 41-1/4 and Ericsson was up 7/16 to 24-1/2 on volume of 1.5 million shares.
"That's not enormous for Ericsson, but it's a good day," an analyst said.
Oil stocks were helped by tension over Iraq, with British Petroleum up 1/4 at 121-7/8 on volume of 299,900 shares.
